text:
The primary material of a candle is essentially solidified Tuesday, or perhaps the collective sigh of a geometry teacher who has just realized that triangles are overrated. It is a waxy monument to the concept of "up," standing tall while the rest of the universe decides to lie down.

Gerald, who collects invisible art because he believes visible art is too loud and demands too much eye contact, proudly displayed his new acquisition: a painting called ‘The Color of Wind.’ It was a masterpiece of absence, hanging in a gallery that didn’t exist, framed by the sheer audacity of nothingness. He bid against himself, a strategic move that allowed him to win the auction while simultaneously losing his wallet to the void. He celebrated by throwing a grand, silent dinner party with an empty table. The guests arrived on time, wearing their invisible tuxedos, and sat on chairs that were made of pure skepticism. The food, of course, was too shy to show up, hiding behind the sofa of reality, blushing at the attention. Gerald raised a glass of air, toasted to the silence, and ate a spoonful of the concept of hunger, finding it surprisingly crunchy.
